description: We are six students passionate about engineering, coding, AI, and mathematics. We joined the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge to explore NASA's lunar missions and use our technical skills to make mission data more accessible, interactive, and engaging while inspiring interest in space exploration.
summary: Payload Pets is a website that turns real NASA CLPS mission data into a game. You adopt a real lunar instrument as a virtual pet and keep it alive through a lunar day by managing sunlight for power, safe temperature, and line of sight to Earth. Our team of six built it at RiverHacks for the NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE 2026, placing 1st in our division. This Lunar mission is simple and fun for everyone.
details: Payload Pets turns real NASA CLPS mission data into a game. Players adopt a real lunar instrument known as a virtual pet and keep it alive through a lunar day by managing sunlight for power, safe temperature, and line of sight to Earth. A Java server calculates Sun and Earth positions for each landing site, and the website turns them into the pet's health. A story mode explains the science along the way. It puts scattered, techinical mission data in one simple place and introduces students and the public to real missions by real aerospace companies. We built it in Java with VS Code and GitHub, using JPL Horizons and NASA CLPS data. What makes it creative is that it uses care and storytelling instead of charts, so abstract data feels personal. We balanced scientific accuracy with simplicity, kept every mission and instrument real, and scoped the project to what our team of six could finish in 48 Hours.
